findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has an inverted, dead feature-flag check and always returns false
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (so `enabled` is true when the flag is OFF) and then returns false on both branches. The feature-flag lookup is dead code and the variable's name means the opposite of its value. The effective behaviour (SQL expressions unconditionally refused) matches the PR's intent, but the code reads as if it were flag-controlled, and the obvious future "fix" of changing the trailing `return false` to `return true` would re-enable SQL expressions precisely when the `sqlExpressions` toggle is disabled. Either reduce the body to a plain `return false` with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264 and the removed DuckDB engine, or fix the inversion if the flag is genuinely meant to be honoured. Relatedly, the `sqlExpressions` toggle stays registered and documented as "enables SQL expressions", so operators who turn it on now get an opaque "sqlExpressions is not implemented" error with nothing explaining why.

findings.title: Legacy SQL command path fails with a misleading user message and spams Error-level logs with raw SQL
findings.body: `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` remain reachable through the legacy rawNode builder (buildCMDNode in nodes.go), which this PR does not gate. They now always fail because `sql.TablesList` calls the stub `DB.RunCommands`, which returns "not implemented". The resulting user-facing error is `errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql", "error reading SQL command")`, which tells the user their SQL is malformed rather than that the feature is disabled, and is inconsistent with the reader.go path ("sqlExpressions is not implemented"). In addition, every evaluation of any dashboard panel or alert rule that still contains a SQL expression now emits an Error-level log from `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:28` (including the full user-supplied SQL and synthesized command) plus a Warn from `sql_command.go:32`, producing persistent error-log noise for an intentionally disabled feature. Short-circuit `NewSQLCommand` with an explicit "SQL expressions are disabled" error before calling `TablesList`, and drop or downgrade the logging.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions are refused regardless of feature flag
findings.body: This change is the in-repo fix for a critical CVE (RCE/LFI via DuckDB SQL expressions), yet no test asserts the new behaviour. There is no test that `ReadQuery` with `type: "sql"` returns an error when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled as well as disabled, nor that `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand` refuse to build a command. Because the gate in `enableSqlExpressions` is written in a confusing, inverted way, a test pinning "SQL query type is rejected with the flag both on and off" is the main protection against the feature being accidentally re-enabled later (e.g. when the `sql.DB` stub is replaced with a real engine) without a security review.
